precepts.text: David gave Solomon the pattern of the porch, the houses, the treasuries, the mercy seat, the courses of the priests and the chariot of the cherubims, all of it by the spirit and in writing by the Lord's hand upon him; the temple's blueprint was David's, Solomon built his father's design.

note.label: The Nativity: the Bloodline, Birthright, & the Messiah

precepts.why:
David, chosen out of Judah and out of his father’s house, hands the building of the house to the son the Lord chose to sit on the throne: “Solomon thy son, he shall build my house and my courts: for I have chosen him to be my son, and I will be his father.” “Moreover I will establish his kingdom for ever”. Solomon’s kingdom, not Solomon and his brethren’s. Then David charges him: “Take heed now; for the Lord hath chosen thee to build an house for the sanctuary: be strong, and do it.”

“Then David gave to Solomon his son the pattern of the porch”. The blueprints to the temple: guess who gave them to Solomon? David. Solomon did not come up with the design; David came up with it, and Solomon fulfilled his father’s wishes. That porch is why the feast of dedication is kept at Solomon’s porch. It took Solomon seven years to build the temple and thirteen years to build his own house, so the temple was done before his house was finished.

David gave him the pattern “of the houses thereof, and of the treasuries thereof, and of the upper chambers thereof”, the floors and levels, “and of the inner parlours thereof, and of the place of the mercy seat”, the holy of holies. “And the pattern of all that he had by the spirit”: the spirit moved David to design the temple. The courses of the priests, which priest for burning incense and which for each service, David was behind all of that too. Gold by weight for the things of gold, “refined gold by weight” for the altar of incense, everything gold, “and gold for the pattern of the chariot of the cherubims, that spread out their wings, and covered the ark of the covenant of the Lord.”

“All this, said David, the Lord made me understand in writing by his hand upon me, even all the works of this pattern.” David did not write it off the top of his head. The Lord moved his hand on what to write, and David drew out the temple through his hands. So the house Solomon built on the throne of the kingdom of the Lord was the Lord’s own pattern, given through David to the son chosen to sit on David’s throne.

precepts.text: Solomon sat upon the throne of the kingdom of the Lord over Israel: Israel is the kingdom of heaven.
precepts.point: The kingdom of heaven that suffers violence is the nation of Israel, the kingdom of the Lord Solomon sat over, and the violent who take it by force were Rome, the same violent man of Psalms 140 and the same man today. What would Jesus say? He called them the violent.

note.label: Zionism in the Face of Syria & Hezbollah

precepts.why:
How is the kingdom of heaven suffering violence? Is somebody jumping up in the sky punching God in the face? No. David answers it: “And of all my sons, (for the Lord hath given me many sons,) he hath chosen Solomon my son to sit upon the throne of the kingdom of the Lord over Israel.” Israel is called the kingdom of the Lord. The throne Solomon sat on was over a nation of people on the earth.

So when Christ says “from the days of John the Baptist until now the kingdom of heaven suffereth violence”, the kingdom of heaven is the nation of Israel. It is our people who suffered the violence.

“and the violent take it by force”. That is Rome. The violent man Christ speaks of is the same one just read in Psalms 140: “preserve me from the violent man; Which imagine mischiefs in their heart; continually are they gathered together for war.” They sharpen their tongues like a serpent, and “adders’ poison is under their lips”: their media, their philosophies, their religions, their politics. They have “purposed to overthrow my goings”, and the one whose goings they overthrow is the Israelites.

It is the same man being violent to us today. So what would Jesus say? He already spoke on it: Christ called Rome the violent man. They are the violent, and the kingdom they take by force is Israel.

precepts.text: The Most High chose Judah, then David's house, then Solomon among David's sons to sit upon the throne of the kingdom of the Lord over Israel.
precepts.point: David repeats the oath he swore by the Lord God of Israel, that Solomon his son shall reign after him and sit upon his throne in his stead. The throne belongs to Solomon by that sworn word.

note.label: 1 Kings 1: A King Exalts Himself and a King Is Anointed

precepts.why:
“Howbeit the Lord God of Israel chose me before all the house of my father to be king over Israel for ever: for he hath chosen Judah to be the ruler; and of the house of Judah, the house of my father; and among the sons of my father he liked me to make me king over all Israel: And of all my sons, (for the Lord hath given me many sons,) he hath chosen Solomon my son to sit upon the throne of the kingdom of the Lord over Israel.”

The Most High chose Judah, then David's house, then Solomon among all David's sons. So when David says, “Assuredly Solomon thy son shall reign after me, and he shall sit upon my throne in my stead”, he is repeating the oath he swore by the Lord God of Israel. The throne belongs to Solomon by that sworn word.

precepts.text: David charged Solomon to know the God of his father and serve him with a perfect heart, for the Lord searcheth all hearts.
precepts.point: David had told Solomon to know the God of his father and serve him with a perfect heart, warning that if he sought Him he would be found, but if he forsook Him he would be cast off. David then gave Solomon the pattern of the porch, the houses, the treasuries, the chambers, and the place of the mercy seat.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 2: Solomon Prepares to Build the House

precepts.why:
“And thou, Solomon my son, know thou the God of thy father, and serve him with a perfect heart and with a willing mind: for the Lord searcheth all hearts.” And David warned him: “if thou seek him, he will be found of thee; but if thou forsake him, he will cast thee off for ever.”

“Solomon determined to build an house for the name of the Lord.” Where did Solomon get this understanding and this vision? It came from his father David, who charged him to build the house.

precepts.text: David gave Solomon the pattern of the porch, the houses, the treasuries, the chambers, and the place of the mercy seat.
precepts.point: David had told Solomon to know the God of his father and serve him with a perfect heart, warning that if he sought Him he would be found, but if he forsook Him he would be cast off. David then gave Solomon the pattern of the porch, the houses, the treasuries, the chambers, and the place of the mercy seat.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 2: Solomon Prepares to Build the House

precepts.why:
“Then David gave to Solomon his son the pattern of the porch, and of the houses thereof, and of the treasuries thereof, and of the upper chambers thereof, and of the inner parlours thereof, and of the place of the mercy seat.”

Solomon did not come up with the house on his own. David charged him to build it and gave him the pattern. So when “Solomon determined to build an house for the name of the Lord”, and told out threescore and ten thousand men to bear burdens, fourscore thousand to hew in the mountain, and three thousand six hundred to oversee them, he was carrying out what his father had given him.

precepts.text: The Most High chose Solomon to sit upon the throne of the kingdom of the Lord over Israel, so the kingdom of God is Israel.
precepts.point: He delivers David from his enemies and lifts him above those that rise against him, delivering him from the violent man. The enemies are not just going to and fro; there is a people who serve satan, the so-called white man, to make it plain.

note.label: Psalm 18: The Song of the Elect in the Last Days

precepts.why:
The kingdom the violent take by force is Israel. David says: “And of all my sons, (for the Lord hath given me many sons,) he hath chosen Solomon my son to sit upon the throne of the kingdom of the Lord over Israel.”

The Most High chose Solomon to sit upon the throne of the kingdom of the Lord over Israel. So the kingdom of God is Israel. When the kingdom of heaven suffers violence in Matthew 11:12, it is Israel suffering the violent man, and it is God that avenges David and subdues the people under him.

precepts.text: The congregation of the Lord in the sight of all Israel; Esau boasts he will rule over the congregation of the Most High in the north, and Israel is the audience of the Bible.
precepts.point: The man of sin has to be revealed, and our people still do not want to acknowledge that Esau is the devil, not Christ. The white picture of Jesus is a deception; the Bible says nothing like that.

note.label: Psalm 52: The Boasting Man of Sin Revealed

precepts.why:
David spoke “in the sight of all Israel the congregation of the Lord, and in the audience of our God”, charging them to “keep and seek for all the commandments of the Lord your God: that ye may possess this good land, and leave it for an inheritance for your children after you for ever.” All Israel is the congregation of the Lord, and Israel is the audience of the Bible.

So when Lucifer says he will sit upon the mount of the congregation in the sides of the north, that is Esau boasting he will rule over the congregation of the Most High, Israel, in the north. He boasts himself in mischief over the very people the Most High gave the commandments and the good land to.

precepts.text: Solomon sat upon the throne of the kingdom of the Lord over Israel, which is what the kingdom is.
precepts.point: The kingdom in view is Israel. The violence is what was done to them, and it is seen plainly in what the Romans did to Jerusalem, taking the kingdom by bloodshed.

note.label: Matthew 11: Art Thou He That Should Come

precepts.why:
“from the days of John the Baptist until now the kingdom of heaven suffereth violence, and the violent take it by force.” The kingdom in view is Israel.

David shows what the kingdom is: “And of all my sons, (for the Lord hath given me many sons,) he hath chosen Solomon my son to sit upon the throne of the kingdom of the Lord over Israel.” The throne Solomon sat on is the throne of the kingdom of the Lord, and that kingdom is over Israel. The kingdom of the Lord and the kingdom of Israel are one and the same.

So the violence the kingdom of heaven suffers is what was done to Israel. It is seen plainly in what the Romans did to Jerusalem, taking the kingdom by bloodshed. The violent took it by force.
